companyDescription: Launch + lunar + defense · Alpha rocket + Blue Ghost lunar lander + SciTec (space domain awareness) · $1.3B backlog, 80% of FY26 revenue already booked · Q2 earnings ~Aug 12
priceNote: Live-prices.json cache (just refreshed, <1h old) — up 1.35% today, a partial recovery from the intraday low reached earlier this morning ($22.27, -7.56%) after yesterday's slide from $25.66. Still well below consensus targets even after the bounce.
summary: Firefly delivered record Q1 2026 revenue ($80.9M) and reaffirmed FY26 guidance of $420-450M with 80% of that already booked and a $1.3B backlog — a well-covered growth story, not a speculative promise. The stock has kept sliding anyway (down another 7.6% today, ~13% below the $25.66 level from 6 days ago), widening the gap to an 11-analyst consensus target of $42.20 (~90% upside). Q2 earnings land ~Aug 12, with the upgraded Alpha Block 2 rocket debut targeted for late summer and Blue Ghost 2 later this year adding real, if imprecisely dated, forward catalysts.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Reports ~Aug 12, 2026. FY26 guidance ($420-450M revenue) is 80% pre-booked via backlog, giving genuine visibility — the print is mainly about execution/margin trajectory rather than a demand question.

catalysts.name: Alpha Block 2 Debut
catalysts.description: Upgraded Alpha rocket configuration — enhanced reliability, increased height, expanded capabilities — targeted for late summer 2026. This is the vehicle upgrade that de-risks Firefly's core launch business after prior Alpha mishaps.

catalysts.name: Blue Ghost 2 Lunar Mission
catalysts.description: Follow-up to Blue Ghost 1's successful Mar 2025 Moon landing (first commercial firm to do so). Blue Ghost 2 targeted for launch as soon as late this year.

risks: Alpha has a real prior mishap history — the upcoming Block 2 debut is explicitly framed as improving reliability after 'explosive mishaps last year,' meaning a repeat failure would hit the stock hard and delay the de-risking narrative
Neither Alpha Block 2 nor Blue Ghost 2 has a precise date ('late summer' / 'late this year') — both can slip, and the dashboard's proximity read on them is necessarily soft
Recent $860M SciTec acquisition (Oct 2025, partly stock-funded at $50/share — well above today's price) adds integration risk and diluted the share count at a much higher valuation than today's
Small-cap, high-beta space name — has fallen further even without new negative company-specific news, suggesting sector-wide risk appetite (not Firefly execution) is currently the dominant driver

Analyst target dispersion is real: consensus $42.20 (11 analysts, high $60/low $28) vs. a separately-cited $48.22 figure — different vintages/methodologies give meaningfully different upside math, worth treating the gate number as approximate

estimateDates.note: 80% of FY26 guide already booked — print is about execution, not demand
De-risks the core launch business post prior-year mishaps

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed holds at 3.50-3.75%, but Chair Warsh's hawkish Jun debut FOMC keeps small-cap, high-beta growth names like FLY exposed to a higher-for-longer repricing more than the broad market.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core PCE accelerated to 3.4% YoY (May) — reinforces the hawkish backdrop into the Jul 28-29 FOMC.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: HIGH — small-cap space/high-beta names have shown real weakness recently even against a resilient broad tape (small caps, speculative growth broadly declined Jul 10 even as the S&P advanced). FLY's continued slide despite in-line fundamentals fits this pattern.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk MEDIUM-HIGH for this name specifically — the backlog/guidance thesis is fundamentals-driven, but FLY's demonstrated small-cap high-beta sensitivity means it's more exposed than most to a risk-off shock around the dense Jul 28-Aug 1 FOMC/earnings/PCE week.
